meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I know who you are, Hale. Owen found out about his zero in class. Explain that.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have on the essay.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing that down. He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in. Show me the screen.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. Pasting from another file proves nothing, Hale.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time. That's a lost mark, not a zero.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what outlines are for. Give me both documents.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Being stuck is what it means, Hale. You cornered a seventeen-year-old without warning and wrote down that he was nervous.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a week at home; of course it's cleaner. Where are you going with all this?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then why say it at all? Your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish anything, so what was the zero standing on on November 3?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Then 4.4 goes in writing, tonight, with the words nothing on his record. Private, not in front of his class, and before I agree to anything I see every document you just described.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. The documents first, Hale.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
You've stepped around that twice now. No dates until I've read them.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
We haven't agreed to anything. You've described papers you still haven't put on this desk.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Who else at this school has seen this, and is anything sitting on his file right now?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered Owen a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, with its mark replacing the zero and a written commitment that nothing goes on his record. Before I agree to anything I want to see every document you described, and I want to know who else at the school has seen this and whether anything is on his file now. I expect that commitment in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she heard you offer the private 4.4 rewrite in writing but never accepted it, and she still wants to see your documents and know whether anything is on his file, so the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4, was in reach but not reached before you ended the meeting.
What moved her: You committed to procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, which met the one demand she would never trade.
What cost ground: You described the version history, outline, note and in-class piece but never put any of them in front of her, even after she asked twice, then moved on to scheduling and to summarising a deal she had not made.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placing the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due came very close to that night, which proves nothing about the essay but is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she told you to show her the screen after the version history, turn it and walk her through the times yourself, and answer her claim that he pasted it from another file, before you move to the next piece.
